summary: Northbridge Support: quality regression after Optimize applied quantization profile (format/accuracy drift on chat + structured output)
description:
Issue summary:
- Customer reports a noticeable quality regression after accepting an Optimize recommendation that changed quantization profile on their dedicated endpoint.
- Primary symptoms: increased JSON/structured-output formatting failures, higher refusal rate on tool-calling prompts, and degraded factual consistency on a subset of their support automation flows.

Customer impact:
- Production impact on Northbridge Support’s “Agent Assist” workflow. They estimate ~8–12% of requests required manual correction due to malformed JSON or missing required keys.
- Customer paused further Optimize changes and requested root-cause + prevention.

Environment:
- Dedicated endpoint: nb-support-prod (us-east)
- Model: llama-3.1-70b-instruct (pinned model version unchanged)
- Change applied via Optimize Console: quantization profile update (FP16 -> INT8 profile)
- Time window of reported regression: 2025-01-16 18:40–22:10 UTC (first noticed shortly after apply)

What changed:
- Optimize recommended applying quantization profile "int8_kv_awq_v2" (customer wording: “new quant profile”).
- No prompt/template changes on customer side.

Steps to reproduce (from customer + Support repro):
1) Send structured-output requests (schema-enforced JSON) to route /v1/chat/completions with response_format=json_schema.
2) Compare before/after the Optimize apply event.
3) After quantization change, model more frequently:
   - returns trailing commentary around JSON
   - omits required fields ("resolution_code")
   - returns invalid JSON (unescaped newlines)

Observed behavior:
- Increased invalid JSON rate and occasional tool-call argument corruption (incorrect escaping / truncated args).
- Customer also flagged “more confident but wrong” answers on a factual QA prompt set.

Expected behavior:
- Optimize changes should not materially degrade response quality; if risk exists, should be gated by evals and/or have an easy rollback with auditability.

Artifacts / logs (internal):
- Optimize apply event (control plane): optimize_apply_20250116T1842Z_nb_support_prod
- Config delta: quant_profile: fp16_default -> int8_kv_awq_v2
- Sample request IDs (redacted): req_01J3NB***, req_01J3NC***
- Support captured 25 failing examples in the secure support bucket (see internal link in comment thread).

Initial hypothesis:
- Quantization profile introduces format drift (structured output + tool-call arguments), likely due to sensitivity in token-level probabilities around punctuation/escaping for this model family under the selected profile.
- This is consistent with known failure modes: formatting drift and reasoning degradation on long-context + schema-constrained prompts.

Requested outcome:
- Provide root-cause analysis, recommended mitigation/rollback, and prevention plan. Customer explicitly asked whether Redwood has a plan to require quality checks before applying Optimize changes and how audit logs will reflect those checks.
comments:
2025-01-16 19:05 UTC — Owen Phillips (Support):
Customer (Northbridge Support) reports quality regression starting ~30 min after they clicked “Apply recommendation” in Optimize (quantization). Symptoms mainly around structured output JSON breaking + some factual drift. They’re asking us to confirm what changed + provide a safe rollback. I’m pulling the Optimize apply audit entry and requesting examples.

Customer quote: “Nothing else changed on our end; after Optimize applied the new quant profile our JSON started failing in prod.”

2025-01-16 19:28 UTC — Diego Ramos (Eng, Rollback/quality signals):
Found the apply event in control plane: optimize_apply_20250116T1842Z_nb_support_prod. Quant profile flipped fp16_default -> int8_kv_awq_v2. No routing or batching changes.

Immediate mitigation: recommend customer roll back quant profile to fp16_default and pin Optimize to “recommend only” until we complete investigation. I can also force a rollback from our side if they want.

Starting internal diff eval now using a small sentinel suite for structured output + tool calling. Will share run IDs.

2025-01-16 20:11 UTC — Sean Gallagher (SRE):
No platform-wide incident detected. Dedicated cluster us-east looks healthy (latency/5xx within normal). This looks like a config-quality issue rather than availability.

If customer needs immediate relief, rollback is low-risk and should not require capacity changes (fp16 uses more GPU, but their reserved pool has headroom).

2025-01-16 20:47 UTC — Selene Huang (Applied ML / Quality guardrails):
We’ve seen this class of regression with quantization transitions on formatting-sensitive tasks. Two known failure modes:
1) “JSON leakage” (extra text outside JSON)
2) Escaping / quoting errors in tool-call args

Please run our internal eval suite tags: structured_output:json_schema + tool_calling:strict_args on both configs. If possible, include a minimum sample size; otherwise at least directional signal.

This is exactly the type of change we want to gate behind mandatory evals (quantization-guardrails-policy proposal in Confluence).

2025-01-16 22:03 UTC — Diego Ramos (Eng):
Internal eval runs complete (subset, n=120 prompts, 3 seeds). Results show statistically meaningful regression on formatting metrics.

Eval run IDs:
- Baseline (fp16_default): evalrun_6f3a1c2c_nb_fp16_20250116
- Candidate (int8_kv_awq_v2): evalrun_9b0d77af_nb_int8_20250116

Key deltas (candidate vs baseline):
- json_schema_valid_rate: 0.941 -> 0.862 (-7.9pp)
- tool_args_parse_success: 0.973 -> 0.905 (-6.8pp)
- rubric_task_success (internal rubric): 0.812 -> 0.786 (-2.6pp)

Notes:
- Failures skew toward long responses and prompts with nested objects/arrays.
- Latency improved ~18% and cost improved ~23%, but quality regression is not acceptable for this workload.

Recommendation: rollback quantization for this tenant; add them to “quantization exclusions” until we have guardrails gating + a safer profile for llama-3.1-70b-instruct.

Also: customer asked for auditability. Today we can show an OptimizeConfigChange audit event (who/when/what), but we do NOT currently log “eval suite ran + pass/fail” because it wasn’t required. This ticket should be linked as motivating case for guardrails gating.

2025-01-17 00:22 UTC — Owen Phillips (Support):
Shared mitigation plan with customer:
- Roll back quant profile to fp16_default immediately (they confirmed they can tolerate cost increase short-term)
- Disable auto-apply / keep Optimize in “recommend only”

Customer asks:
1) Can Redwood block these changes automatically in the future if quality checks fail?
2) Can Redwood provide audit logs proving an eval ran before config changes?

I told them we’re implementing guardrails gating and will follow up with timelines + how they can provide prompt sets.

2025-01-17 02:10 UTC — Diego Ramos (Eng):
Rollback executed on their dedicated endpoint at 2025-01-17 02:05 UTC. Monitoring:
- json_schema_valid_rate back to baseline range within ~30 minutes
- Customer-reported failures stopped (pending their morning confirmation)

Action items (internal):
- Add tenant-level blocklist for int8_kv_awq_v2 on llama-3.1-70b-instruct until a safer transition is validated.
- Feed the failing examples into quantization regression corpus (secure).
- Propose mandatory suite list for quantization applies (structured_output + tool_calling + long_context slice).

This aligns with upcoming work in quantization guardrails policy + Optimize gating enforcement.

2025-01-20 16:43 UTC — Jonas Weber (Applied ML / Evals program lead):
Adding this to the set of real-world regressions to calibrate thresholds. Proposed quantization gating requirements (draft):
- Hard requirements for any quantization profile change:
  - json_schema_valid_rate: no more than -1.0pp vs baseline (min n=200)
  - tool_args_parse_success: no more than -1.0pp vs baseline (min n=200)
  - rubric_task_success: no more than -0.5pp vs baseline (CI-based rule)
- If baseline unavailable, run baseline+candidate back-to-back and persist artifacts.

We should incorporate Northbridge’s prompt patterns if they’re willing to share a sanitized prompt set. Owen: please ask if they can provide 200–500 prompts under NDA; we’ll provide a redaction template.

2025-01-22 09:12 UTC — Owen Phillips (Support):
Customer confirmed rollback resolved issue. They’re open to participating as a design partner for the guardrails gating pilot, subject to prompt redaction workflow.

Closing ticket as Resolved. Follow-ups tracked separately under the guardrails project; customer wants audit logs and prevention as part of their renewal conversation.
resolution: Resolved via rollback of Optimize-applied quantization profile (int8_kv_awq_v2 -> fp16_default) on dedicated endpoint. Internal eval runs confirmed regression on structured output + tool calling metrics. Preventive actions proposed: introduce mandatory guardrails gating for quantization transitions (eval suite + thresholds) and add model/tenant exclusions for known-unsafe profile transitions until validated. Customer invited to pilot guardrails gating and provide sanitized prompt sets for improved coverage.
